dct_description_sm: Description of past variability in benthic community structure may help to track future potential modifications brought about by changes experienced at large scales in the Arctic environment. We use multivariate analysis to reveal or illustrate patterns in diversity and species richness where univariate analyses cannot. Multivariate analyses are more robust at detecting transformations that can occur in species abundance and dominance in a community. Applying such tools to historical data may provide insights into the state of historical communities. There has been a progressive thinning and shorter duration of sea ice cover in the Arctic in general and in many of the Canadian Arctic regions. This, coupled with the likely future exploitation of the Canadian Arctic for marine transport, has created a need to establish baseline data on the state of the marine environment using new statistical tools for comparisons with contemporary studies. The objectives of this paper were to use such data to: (1) characterize and evaluate differences in benthic macrofaunal species richness, α, β and γ diversity, and assemblages from historic data sets within the Canadian Arctic regions; (2) compare the relative importance of spatial and temporal variability of species assemblages from those sites with temporal data; and (3) evaluate the correlation between benthic assemblages and the environmental variables for which we have good information.
dct_title_s: Biodiversity of benthic assemblages on the Arctic continental shelf: historical data from Canada
